title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Abolishing Certain Judicial Interpretations Issued between 1979 and 1989
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Abolishing Certain Judicial Interpretations Issued Between 1979 and 1989

Fa Fa [1996] No. 34

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

After publishing the first batch of the catalogue of judicial interpretations to be abolished, our Court proceeded to conduct a comprehensive review of the judicial interpretations issued between 1979 and 1989. We are now issuing to you the second batch of the catalogue of judicial interpretations that, following discussion and decision by the Judicial Committee of our Court, are to be abolished. This batch of abolished judicial interpretations totals 69 items, including 16 in the area of criminal adjudication, 34 in the area of civil adjudication, and 19 in the area of economic adjudication. Among them, a few documents were issued in the form of "letters" or "replies." Considering that these documents have the nature of judicial interpretations and played a role in guiding adjudicative work at the time, and in the spirit of respecting history and maintaining the original appearance, they are also being included in this review as judicial interpretations. The abolished judicial interpretations shall no longer apply from the date hereof (some have already become invalid on their own). However, judgments and rulings made in the past in applying the aforementioned judicial interpretations to relevant cases remain valid. The work of reviewing judicial interpretations will continue. Where judicial interpretation documents jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court and relevant departments need to be abolished, our Court will jointly issue documents with the relevant departments to abolish them. Judicial interpretations in which only part of the content is no longer suitable for current adjudicative practice are not included in this review; our Court will organize relevant departments to study and amend them on the basis of a comprehensive review. Please promptly report any opinions from your localities to our Court.

December 31, 1996

Appendix: Catalogue of Judicial Interpretations Issued Between 1979 and 1989 That the Supreme People's Court Decided to Abolish (Second Batch)
